input.question: How do LLM agents improve on later attempts using feedback or memory, without updating their weights?

supporting.quote: Reflexion agents verbally reflect on task feedback signals, then maintain their own reflective text in an episodic memory buffer to induce better decision-making in subsequent trials
supporting.why: Reflexion stores verbal reflections in memory.

supporting.quote: learning from agent experiences without requiring parametric updates
supporting.why: ExpeL learns from experience without parametric updates.

supporting.quote: SELF-REFINE does not require any supervised training data, additional training, or reinforcement learning
supporting.why: Self-Refine improves outputs with self-feedback and no training.

supporting.quote: an ever-growing skill library of executable code for storing and retrieving complex behaviors
supporting.why: Voyager reuses a growing skill library.

draft_answer: Agents keep verbal reflections, extracted insights, self-feedback, or skill libraries in memory or context and reuse them on later attempts, with no weight updates.
